reason: 'The first push into Roman land had gone unanswered, so the tribes along the borders pushed harder... until the whole western half came apart.' Rome fought back against barbarian incursions for centuries (e.g. 3rd-century wars, Adrianople 378, Catalaunian Plains 451; source: Wikipedia, Fall of the Western Roman Empire); the fall was not caused by an unanswered first push.

'if being busy beat being hungry, then work was rest. He helped Grandma sweep the porch, carried the chairs out' on Yom Kippur. Yom Kippur is a sabbath of rest on which work is forbidden (Leviticus 23:28-32, KJV via BibleGateway); calling work 'rest' misstates the observance the story is meant to explain.

The story conveys the Orthodox belief in resurrection, but never names Reform Judaism; the other view is only 'at our synagogue, our rabbi says', so the fact's Orthodox-versus-Reform contrast is not conveyed.
'So the blockage was puffy, swollen walls, not a pile of gunk' and 'It's not a mucus problem.' The fact says swelling is the main cause, not the only one; mucus also contributes.
'Combines can't get this close to the fence,' said about a kale field. Combines harvest grain; mature kale is harvested by hand (source: andnowuknow.com, Church Brothers Farms on kale harvesting).

'when the narrator finds him under the tree with his neck bent.' In Hurst's story the narrator finds Doodle beneath a red nightshade bush beside the road, not under a tree (source: literariness.org analysis / enotes).

'Ms. Ortiz got 34 percent, Mr. Bell got 33 percent, and Ms. Grant got 33 percent, and Grant won.' Under first-past-the-post the 34% candidate (Ortiz) wins; a 33% candidate cannot beat a 34% one, so the vote-splitting example is wrong.

'The points fell into a straight line... which matched the way her bulb pushed back against the flow.' The story ties a straight, through-zero V-I line to the bulb, but a filament bulb is non-ohmic and its V-I graph curves as the filament heats (source: savemyexams / miniphysics I-V graph notes).

'20 S, 70 W, Atacama, zero rain ever' and 'a place with no rain at all' are left as the takeaway. The fact is that only some weather stations in parts of the Atacama have never recorded rain; the desert as a whole does get occasional rain.

'Each answer came out correct, and each time the fraction was bigger than it needed to be.' Multiplying denominators does not always give a larger-than-needed denominator; in Marcus's own example, 3 x 1 = 3 is already the least common denominator. His step 'three times one gives me three over one' is also garbled.

The numbers contradict each other: 'Kelsey Okafor had scored nineteen goals this season' but the site lists her '46 for 61' and 'Kelsey made forty-six'. In soccer, shots made are goals, so she cannot have both 19 goals and 46 made shots.

'The stadium claim... was only mostly wrong' and it was rated 'Half True', yet the real figure was $10 against a claimed $2,000. On PolitiFact's Truth-O-Meter, a mostly wrong claim rates Mostly False (or False), and Half True means partially accurate (source: PolitiFact rating definitions, via WRAL 'How we determine Truth-O-Meter ratings').

'if his dad had stopped growing at fourteen, and his uncle at seventeen, then the family plates closed late... Late closers, all of them.' A boy who stops growing at 14 has growth plates that closed early, not late, so the story endorses a wrong conclusion about growth.

'pulled down on the rope. The stone rose, the bucket swung up over the bank.' On a shaduf, pulling the bucket end down raises the counterweight; the full bucket is lifted when the counterweight comes back down, so the stone and the bucket cannot rise together.
The story shows Levi replacing 'um' with a silent pause, but it never says that the pause makes a speaker sound more confident or gives listeners time to take in the point.

'She carried the board to the far corner of the yard, upwind of Marcus, so any gas drifting off would blow away from him.' If she is upwind of Marcus, the wind carries the gas toward him; she needed to be downwind.

'he suspected they were still running in the background ... Still twenty minutes left, all twenty.' Phone screen-time reports count foreground use while the screen is on, not apps idling in the background, so swiping apps away does not stop time accruing (and 9 minutes already used cannot leave all twenty).

'one phrase kept appearing: accept the offer.' 'Accept the offer'/'yes, and' is later improv vocabulary (Del Close, Keith Johnstone), not Spolin's; Spolin spoke of group agreement (spolin.com, 'The Difference between Spolin Games and Popular Improv').
'a raccoon ... strictly nocturnal.' Raccoons are mainly nocturnal but not strictly; daytime activity is normal (wildlife sources, e.g. skedaddlewildlife.com).
'Where I grew up, in Antarctica's dry valleys.' The McMurdo Dry Valleys have no permanent residents; nobody grows up there.
The story never mentions adrenaline; 'Your heart goes fast and it pulls blood away from your stomach' omits the hormone that causes both and reads as if the heart pulls the blood away.

'It was written before group chats even existed.' Multi-user chat (IRC, 1988) predates RFC 1855, which has its own section on IRC/real-time services; its author was Sally Hambridge, not 'this guy' (rfc-editor.org RFC 1855).

'She sketched five quick boxes on the back of the flyer, doubling her totals in her head.' Compound interest on a savings account does not double the balance each year; each year adds interest at the stated rate on the current balance.

The story never says the shaded top result is a paid ad or that paid ads sit above unpaid results; it only says the first link was not trustworthy. (Also, 'one column for each bag' conflicts with summing a single column to get the total.)

'Cairo's tall bar stopped at about 40' mm in March, on an axis to 300 mm, looking taller than Singapore's 170 on a 400 mm axis. Cairo gets about 4 mm of rain in March (WeatherSpark, meteonews.ch climate tables), and 40/300 of an axis is a shorter bar than 170/400, so the story's example of the scale trick is wrong.

'At 20 meters, a small delay in hearing go added a real chunk of error to every run' and the echo test 'matched the rule: about 0.6 meters per second for every degree.' Sound crosses 20 m in about 0.06 s at any room temperature, and a few degrees change that by under a millisecond, far too small to explain a slow marble or to measure with a hand stopwatch.

The story conveys only that the British call it the 'Mexican wave'; it never says the wave became known worldwide at the 1986 FIFA World Cup in Mexico, which is why it has that name (source: Wikipedia, Wave (audience)).

The story says a 'for week in weeks' line followed by an unindented print line runs and prints only the last row. With no indented body, Python raises IndentationError ('expected an indented block') and prints nothing (source: Python docs, Lexical analysis: Indentation).
'Tyler added text-align: centre to the heading ... and watched the title glide to the middle.' CSS accepts only the spelling 'center'; 'centre' is invalid and is ignored (source: MDN, text-align).

'Nine-year-olds can't just walk in.' PG-13 is only a caution to parents; it does not restrict admission of children under 13 (source: Wikipedia, MPA film rating system). The July 1, 1984 date is stated correctly.

'Over the water a little wheel of paper had spun because air was rising there and pulling air in from the sand side.' Air rises over the warmer sand/land, and surface air flows in from the cooler water side (source: Wikipedia, Sea breeze). The Köppen fact itself is stated correctly.
